metamorphosis.name: Metamorphosis
metamorphosis.blurb: Some animals change body form completely as they grow up, like a mealworm becoming a beetle.
metamorphosis.subject: biology
aliases: how does a caterpillar become a butterfly
why do tadpoles turn into frogs

The hormones in charge of a bug's moult and a tadpole's change.

morphogen-gradient.name: Morphogen gradients
morphogen-gradient.blurb: A signal spreads from a source and gives cells different instructions depending on how much of it they get.
morphogen-gradient.subject: biology
aliases: how do cells know where they are in an embryo

A morphogen spreads from its source by diffusion, so distance from the source sets how much a cell receives.

neural-crest.name: The neural crest
neural-crest.blurb: A band of cells at the edge of the neural plate leaves, travels through the embryo and forms many tissues.
neural-crest.subject: biology
aliases: where do pigment cells and gut neurons come from
cells that leave the neural tube and migrate

near.why: Crest cells form at the edges of the plate that folds up into the neural tube.

Crest cells leave the sheet by loosening their hold on their neighbours.
Crest cells make support cells that wrap nerves, as well as sensory neurons outside the brain.

neural-induction.name: Neural induction (the default model)
neural-induction.blurb: In frog embryos, the outer layer of cells becomes nervous system wherever the skin signal BMP is blocked.
neural-induction.subject: biology
aliases: how does the embryo decide which cells become the nervous system

The cells told to become nervous system next fold into the neural tube.

neural-stem-cells.name: Neural stem cells (radial glia)
neural-stem-cells.blurb: Stem cells in the developing brain divide to renew themselves and to make the neurons the brain needs.
neural-stem-cells.subject: biology
aliases: where do the brain's neurons come from

A few places in the adult brain keep stem cells that still make new neurons.

neural-tube-defects.name: Neural tube defects
neural-tube-defects.blurb: When part of the neural tube fails to close, that stretch of brain or spinal cord stays open at birth.
neural-tube-defects.subject: biology
aliases: folic acid and neural tube defects
what happens when the neural tube does not close

Another way a developing brain goes wrong: too few neurons are made, though the tube closed.

neurulation.name: Neurulation (forming the neural tube)
neurulation.blurb: A flat plate of cells on the embryo's back narrows, folds and seals into the tube that becomes brain and spinal cord.
neurulation.subject: biology

organizer.name: Organizers (signaling centers in the embryo)
organizer.blurb: An organizer is a small group of embryo cells whose signals tell nearby cells which body parts to build, and where.
organizer.subject: biology
aliases: how did a graft make a second body axis

Sonic hedgehog from the floor plate acts as a local organizer in the neural tube.

outer-radial-glia.name: Outer radial glia
outer-radial-glia.blurb: Outer radial glia are brain stem cells that divide far from the ventricle and are plentiful in humans and other primates.
outer-radial-glia.subject: biology
aliases: a second site where brain stem cells divide

Faults in dividing progenitors leave a small cortex, which shows how much depends on these cells.

planar-cell-polarity.name: Planar cell polarity
planar-cell-polarity.blurb: Cells in a flat sheet agree on which way is which, so structures such as hairs all point one way.
planar-cell-polarity.subject: biology

how cells in a sheet line up

When cells in the neural plate lose their shared direction, the tube can fail to close.
The hairs on the inner ear's hair cells all lean the same way because of planar polarity.

pregnancy.name: Pregnancy and birth
pregnancy.blurb: The placenta supplies the fetus with food and oxygen and makes hormones, while the mother's body adjusts until labour begins.
pregnancy.subject: biology

The embryo that settles in the womb began as a fertilized egg dividing and moving cells inside.

proneural-genes.name: Proneural genes
proneural-genes.blurb: Proneural genes give a cluster of cells the ability to become neurons and push them toward that fate.
proneural-genes.subject: biology

reelin.name: Reelin and the reeler mouse
reelin.blurb: Reelin is a protein secreted by cells at the top of the cortex that neurons need to take their places.
reelin.subject: biology

retinoic-acid-signaling.name: Retinoic acid as a body-axis signal
retinoic-acid-signaling.blurb: A vitamin A product made toward the back of the embryo shifts cells toward a more tail-like identity.
retinoic-acid-signaling.subject: biology

sexual-differentiation.name: Becoming male or female (sexual differentiation)

temporal-identity.name: Birth time sets neuron identity (temporal identity)

birth-dating-cells.name: Birth dating cells (BrdU labelling)

calcium-imaging.name: Calcium imaging

cell-fractionation.name: Cell fractionation

chi-square-test.name: The chi-square test

chi-square-test.subject: biology

how far can counts stray from a ratio by chance

clinical-trial-evidence.name: Reading a clinical trial

dna-sequencing.name: DNA sequencing

forward-and-reverse-genetics.name: Forward and reverse genetics

genome-assembly.name: Genome assembly and the reference genome

gwas.name: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS)

Many targeted drugs block a kinase, so knowing its real targets explains what the drug does.

lineage-tracing.name: Lineage tracing (which cells came from which)
lineage-tracing.blurb: Scientists mark one cell so that every cell it later makes carries the mark, showing which cells came from which.
lineage-tracing.subject: biology
aliases: how do scientists trace where a cell came from

rungs.adds: Quail grafts, then Cre reporters and barcodes, mark one founder's whole family of cells.

near.why: Marking one stem cell shows which specialized cells it makes and how long it keeps renewing.
A marked mutant cell's family can be followed as it spreads through healthy tissue.
Cre and lox in mice switch on a permanent mark in only the chosen cells.
Tracing follows which cell a cell came from; birth dating tells when it was made.

mark-recapture.name: Counting hidden animals (mark and recapture)
mark-recapture.blurb: Ecologists mark some animals, catch a second sample, and use the share already marked to estimate how many there are.
mark-recapture.subject: biology
aliases: how to count animals you cannot all see

rungs.adds: Mark 10, recatch 10, find 2 marked: estimate 50; missed sites need repeat visits.

near.why: To say whether a population is growing or shrinking, you first need a count of how many there are.
Marked animals that are never caught again are a reminder that every survey misses some animals.
An estimate of how many animals there are feeds the survival and birth counts of a life table.

microscopy.name: Microscopes: magnification and resolution
microscopy.blurb: A microscope enlarges small things, but shows a detail only if it is wider than the smallest gap the tool can separate.
microscopy.subject: biology
aliases: why can't a light microscope see a virus

rungs.adds: Eyepiece times objective: 10 × 40 is 400x, which shows yeast's oval shape.
Eye 0.1 mm, light microscope 0.2 µm, electron microscope 1 to 2 nm.
520 nm light and NA 1.40 give 227 nm, so 150 nm vesicles blur.

near.why: Looking at cork and pond water through lenses is how people first saw that living things are made of cells.
Most cells are far too small to see without a microscope, which is a result of why cells stay small.
Magnifying a cell shows the small parts inside it, each with its own job.
Overlapping colours in an image are easy to over-read, because resolution limits what close together means.

needed-versus-enough.name: Needed versus enough (necessity and sufficiency)
needed-versus-enough.blurb: Taking a part away shows whether it is needed; switching it on by itself shows whether it is enough.
needed-versus-enough.subject: biology
aliases: what a lesion study can show
does a lesion show where a memory is stored
loss of function versus gain of function

rungs.adds: Cerebellar removal abolished the rabbit's learned blink: needed, but not shown stored.
Light on tagged dentate cells made mice freeze: enough, but not shown needed.
Muscimol in MT impaired motion judgments; in LIP it did not.
Gain of function tests sufficiency, loss tests necessity; name cells, projection, timing, behaviour.
NGF injected enlarges ganglia; antiserum to NGF destroys them in newborn mice.

near.why: Driving chosen cells with light tests whether they are enough, and silencing them tests whether they are needed.
Removing a protein shows it is needed, and putting it back shows whether the effect returns.
A brain area's firing can follow a decision closely while silencing it leaves the choice intact.
A lesion that removes a memory shows a structure is needed, not that the memory is stored there.

optogenetics.name: Optogenetics
optogenetics.blurb: A light-gated channel from a microbe is placed in chosen cells, so a flash of light switches those cells on or off.
optogenetics.subject: biology
aliases: how do scientists switch neurons on with light

rungs.adds: Construct-by-light two-by-two: light alone changed firing in mice with no opsin.
Channelrhodopsin-2: blue flashes make hippocampal neurons fire, millisecond by millisecond.

near.why: Blue flashes make neurons fire nerve pulses in step with the light.
The tool is a channel from a microbe that opens in light and lets ions flow, like any pore in a membrane.
Switching cells on with light tests whether they are enough, and switching them off tests whether they are needed.
Light-gated channels placed in surviving eye cells are being tried to bring back some sight after photoreceptors die.

organoids.name: Organoids (brains in a dish)
organoids.blurb: Stem cells grown in a dish organize themselves into small tissue that resembles part of an organ.
organoids.subject: biology
aliases: growing a brain in a dish

rungs.adds: Progenitor zones form around cavities, but blood vessels and most layers do not.

near.why: Organoids grow from stem cells that renew themselves and make specialized cells.
A patient's skin cells can be reset to stem cells and grown into an organoid carrying that patient's genes.
Brain organoids from patient cells let scientists watch how a small cortex forms when dividing cells fail.

pcr.name: PCR (polymerase chain reaction)
pcr.blurb: A tube of DNA, two primers and a heat-stable enzyme copy one chosen region, doubling it each cycle.
pcr.subject: biology
aliases: how do scientists copy DNA in a tube

rungs.adds: Two inward-facing primers double a region each cycle; lower Ct means more template.

near.why: PCR is DNA copying done in a tube: each strand gets a new partner, and primers mark where to start.
Cloning makes copies by letting bacteria grow, which suits long pieces and lasting stocks of DNA.
PCR copies the trace of DNA in a water sample until it is plentiful enough to detect.

perturbation-and-rescue.name: Remove it, then put it back (rescue experiments)
perturbation-and-rescue.blurb: To show a protein causes an effect, remove it, then restore it and see if the effect returns.
perturbation-and-rescue.subject: biology
aliases: how do we show a protein causes a defect

rungs.adds: Silence it, then restore an RNAi-resistant copy: only then blame the protein.

near.why: A rescue adds the missing step: removing a part shows it is needed, and restoring it shows the cause.
A knockout mouse removes a gene, and putting the gene back is the rescue.
Putting two mutations in one cell and checking whether it works shows which gene each one hit.

protein-purification.name: Protein purification
protein-purification.blurb: To study one protein, scientists track it with a test of what it does, then remove everything else step by step.
protein-purification.subject: biology
aliases: how to find a molecule you cannot see

rungs.adds: Specific activity climbs from 10 to 30,000 units/mg across a purification table.
Dilute twofold from 1:250, then divide units by protein to track purification.

near.why: After purifying a protein you still have to show which protein it is, using a gel, an antibody and its pieces.
The survival factor for young nerve cells was found and purified by following its effect step by step.
Tracking an enzyme through each step uses its activity as the test, because enzymes make reactions go.
Breaking cells open and spinning the pieces apart is often where a purification begins.

pulse-chase.name: Pulse-chase labelling
pulse-chase.blurb: Label one batch of new protein for a moment, then follow it to learn the order of its stops.
pulse-chase.subject: biology
aliases: how do we know the route a protein takes
tracking a protein through the cell over time

rungs.adds: Guinea pig pancreas: a three-minute pulse, then ER, Golgi, granules in order.

near.why: Following labelled protein revealed its route from the rough ER through the Golgi to the cell surface.
A labelled batch also shows how long a protein lasts before the cell destroys it.
Spinning cells into parts at each time shows which part the labelled protein has reached.

radioimmunoassay.name: Measuring a hormone by competition (radioimmunoassay)
radioimmunoassay.blurb: A hormone in a sample competes with a labelled copy for scarce antibody, so less label bound means more hormone.
radioimmunoassay.subject: biology
aliases: how to measure a hormone at tiny concentrations

rungs.adds: Insulin at tens of picomolar: unlabelled hormone competes with labelled copy for antibody.

near.why: Measuring a hormone is the first step in locating a failed link in a hormone chain.
How much label stays bound depends on how tightly the antibody holds the hormone, which Kd measures.
The scarce antibody in the test is a molecule the immune system makes to recognise one target.
This method was first used to measure insulin in blood, which showed how blood sugar control works.

single-cell-rna-seq.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing
single-cell-rna-seq.blurb: Counting the RNA of each cell separately shows the mix of cell types and states that a bulk sample averages.
single-cell-rna-seq.subject: biology
aliases: why a bulk measurement can mislead

rungs.adds: Clusters are hypotheses: cell type, passing state or artifact, tested by lineage tracing.

near.why: Cells with the same DNA make different RNA, and this method reads that difference cell by cell.
A brain atlas sorts cells into types by the genes they use, which is read from each cell's RNA.
Touch, pain and itch neurons were told apart by which genes each one uses.
Reading cells one at a time can show mutant cells hidden in healthy tissue that a bulk sample would average away.

transgenic-and-knockout-mice.name: Transgenic and knockout mice (Cre and lox)
transgenic-and-knockout-mice.blurb: Scientists add, remove or change a gene in a mouse, and with Cre and lox they do it only in chosen cells.
transgenic-and-knockout-mice.subject: biology

rungs.adds: Transgenes, knock-ins and Cre at loxP put a tool into one cell type.
Cre cuts a floxed gene only where it runs; reporter light is not deletion.

near.why: Knocking out a chosen gene to see what changes is reverse genetics, done in a whole animal.
Adding, removing or changing a gene in a mouse uses the same cutting and joining tools as other gene editing.
Cre and lox can switch on a lasting mark in chosen cells, so their descendants can be followed.
Putting the gene back into a knockout mouse tests whether the missing gene caused the effect.
